title: Dirty rice
subtitle: Cajun rice with chicken liver, pork mince, and the holy trinity
excerpt: Dirty rice is a Cajun side dish of long-grain rice cooked with finely chopped chicken livers, pork mince, the Cajun trinity, and spices. The chopped livers turn the rice a dark, mottled colour and give it an intense, savoury flavour. It takes about 30 minutes and pairs with anything from the grill.
sourceNotes: Cajun culinary tradition, Louisiana. Dirty rice is documented in Paul Prudhomme, Chef Paul Prudhomme's Louisiana Kitchen (1984), and in WPA Louisiana Writers' Project food surveys. It is considered a foundational Cajun side dish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 2 months. Reheat with a splash of stock to loosen.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles easily and keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

content.text: Dirty rice gets its name from the colour the chicken livers give the cooked rice: a mottled, muddy brown that looks like dirty rice but tastes intensely savoury. The livers are chopped very finely so they dissolve into the rice rather than appearing as identifiable pieces. Pork mince and the Cajun trinity round out the base.
Brown the meats and cook the trinity

Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in the saucepan over medium-high heat. Add {{pork-mince}} of pork mince and brown well, breaking it up, for 5 minutes. Add the {{chicken-livers}} of finely chopped chicken livers and cook for 3 minutes until they lose their pink colour. Add {{onion}} onion, {{celery}} celery, and {{pepper-green}} green pepper. Cook for 4 minutes. Add {{garlic}} of garlic, {{cayenne-pepper}} of cayenne, {{paprika-smoked}} of smoked paprika, and {{thyme-dried}} of dried thyme.

Add {{long-grain-rice}} of rice and stir to coat. Pour in {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock and bring to a boil. Cover, reduce to the lowest heat, and cook for 18 minutes without lifting the lid. Remove from the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork, season, and serve scattered with spring onions.

items.cause: Heat too high during the covered simmer.
items.fix: The lowest heat the hob allows. A heat diffuser helps if available.
Chop livers to a near-paste before adding. The goal is for them to dissolve into the rice.

content.text: Andouille sausage finely diced can replace the pork mince. A small amount of beef mince adds complexity. Dirty rice is the canonical Cajun accompaniment to fried chicken, blackened catfish, or grilled sausages.

Dirty rice is a Cajun side dish of practical origin. Organ meats that would otherwise be wasted give the rice its colour and depth. It is one of the defining side dishes of the Louisiana table and a regular at Cajun community suppers and church lunches.
